repetition.notes: Opening and phrase counts are literal lexical recurrence; they do not establish visual duplication.

verified_findings.claim: Median length is 25.0 words across all 540 V3 texts versus 45.5 words across the ten authoritative October examples (45.1% lower). Wide V3 texts have a 33.0-word median, so the gap is not solely the close-up cohort.
verified_findings.scope_and_limit: The October set is ten mostly room-level examples without Education/Gaming coverage; length is a specificity signal, not a quality score.

verified_findings.claim: All 270 V3 close-up texts are one sentence; 240/270 explicitly combine a support-surface noun with a light term. Their 19-word median and frozen 0/1 local-prop ceilings explain much of the sparse feel.
verified_findings.scope_and_limit: A lexical construction count does not show whether an image is sparse; close-up brevity is partly intentional camera control.

verified_findings.claim: The October examples concentrate character in coherent clusters such as half-finished coffee, slightly overgrown plants, full shelves, loose papers, pastry crumbs, glasses, and a water glass. V3 more often distributes one paper artifact, one surface material, and one lighting phrase across separate alternatives.
verified_findings.scope_and_limit: This is a corpus-level comparison, not a claim that each October paragraph was directly rewritten into a specific V3 candidate.

verified_findings.claim: Visible human action is nearly absent from V3 prose: the bounded detector finds it in 3/540 V3 texts, while it finds visible people or hands performing tasks in 29/58 allowed lifestyle-column prompts.
verified_findings.scope_and_limit: The close profiles intentionally omit people, and the authoritative October examples themselves contain no visible people; human residue can be safer than adding a person.

verified_findings.claim: V3 does preserve some character through surface wear, material specificity, annotated/folded artifacts, wrappers, and bounded background anchors; the defect is under-combination and repeated sparse formulation, not complete absence of detail.
verified_findings.scope_and_limit: Cue matching is lexical and does not confirm downstream visibility.

highest_value: Mid-use state on an already-allowed artifact: annotated, folded, clipped, half-used, date-stamped, waiting for sign-off.
Use residue on the existing support plane: faint scuffs, softened edge, uneven polish, light stain, paper-edge dust.
A relational state among allowed objects: mug beside marked notes, pen laid across a form, tabbed folder under a clipped proof.
Localized lighting with a plausible source or time cue: warm window falloff, clean overhead task light, late-day side light.
One personal or pause cue within the existing prop budget: half-finished drink, crumbs, wrapper, glasses, or a familiar residential textile edge.
cue_types_to_preserve_character_without_.why: These cues add history and implied human use inside the existing crop and object slots. They do not require a broader room inventory or a larger shot.
cue_types_to_preserve_character_without_.camera_rule: Count a richer modifier or state on an existing object as character, not as permission to add another object. Keep the frozen 0/1/3 local-prop and 0/2 background ceilings until images demonstrate more capacity.

authoritative_before_examples.text: Laptop: A lived-in home workspace with a wooden desk holding an open notebook, spiral pad, loose papers, pens, and a half-finished coffee. Soft daylight filters through large windows and relaxed curtains, with a comfortable chair, slightly overgrown houseplants, full shelving, books, and familiar residential objects throughout the room. Warm, layered, and casually imperfect rather than styled or modern. Minimal blue accents appear naturally in a few small everyday details.
Laptop: A modern coffee shop workspace focused on a lived-in table, with a ceramic coffee cup, notebook, loose papers, pen, glasses, small plate with pastry crumbs, and a water glass.

Three business professionals standing around a wooden desk while engaged in an animated discussion, holding printed documents and gesturing mid-conversation, in a bright, modern office with large windows. A closed NOTEBOOK-Cheddar_13_NB_ANI sits on the desk between them, and papers, a water glass, and notebooks are scattered across the surface. The professionals are dressed in a mix of a grey sweater, a light blue button-down shirt, and a white ruffled blouse, and the environment has soft natural daylight streaming through the office windows, with a city skyline visible outside. Capture the scene from an eye-level medium group shot with shallow depth of field, keeping the three professionals as the sharp visual anchor while the desk and window backdrop are softly blurred.

A warm, modern home office viewed across a large minimalist wooden desk in the foreground. A sculptural contemporary desk lamp casts a soft amber glow beside a matte black coffee mug, while a curved wooden chair sits partially tucked beneath the desk. In the background, a tall white built-in bookshelf is filled with books, storage objects, and a compact printer. A cork bulletin board with casually pinned notes and papers hangs on the wall, adding a subtle lived-in quality. A large window with a dark roller shade occupies one side of the room. Clean architectural lines, natural wood, warm neutral tones, soft indirect lighting, and understated residential details create a sophisticated yet comfortable workspace. Photorealistic interior photography, cinematic evening light, gentle shadows, shallow atmospheric depth, uncluttered composition, contemporary Scandinavian-inspired styling.

visual_review_observations_2026_10_26: The laptop close composite is dominated by the open Koki laptop across the center-right and lower canvas; there is little credible local room inventory without changing framing.

The printer close composite is dominated by the tall Magic printer body; a single compact paper/workflow artifact can plausibly sit adjacent, while a person or background fixture would imply more scene than this crop establishes.

Both wide composites place a much smaller product left of center with a large transparent field; this creates room for scene context but does not prove that every blank pixel is usable floor, tabletop, wall, or background.
The laptop is materially smaller in its wide composite than the printer in its wide composite, so dense foreground detail is especially likely to overpower laptop legibility.

limitations: Alpha occupancy describes the supplied transparent product render, not usable scene geometry or post-composition salience.
The four renders are a purposive sample of one Koki laptop and the only durable high-resolution effective printer, Magic; they do not represent every SKU or camera direction.
The review composites contain the product on a neutral background, not generated lifestyle scenes; object placement feasibility remains a design hypothesis until image generation.
No segmentation, occlusion, or product-salience metric was computed for generated outputs.

contradictions_and_alternatives.observation: V3 includes many material, wear, and paper-state details, including selected examples with scuffed surfaces, marked-up documents, pinned notices, wrappers, and waiting-for-sign-off states.
contradictions_and_alternatives.implication: C-Tech's concern cannot be reduced to a binary missing-keyword problem; combination, coherence, and repeated surface-light syntax are plausible causes.

contradictions_and_alternatives.alternative: The downstream rewriter or image model may suppress or homogenize character even when upstream text contains it.
contradictions_and_alternatives.test: Use the same 108-row sampling structure and compare selected upstream prompt, downstream rewrite, and output image with cue-survival annotations.

contradictions_and_alternatives.alternative: The ten October examples may feel richer mainly because they are room-level compositions and are not camera-matched to tight product renders.
contradictions_and_alternatives.test: Evaluate close and wide rows separately, retaining the four exact tags and frozen ceilings; do not demand October-level room inventories from close crops.

recommended_validation_gate.next_test: For each of the four tags, annotate the 108 V4 texts and images for cue survival, product salience, occlusion, and unintended shot widening. Compare against matched V3 rows by view, not only aggregate diversity.
pass_signals: More coherent mid-use or personal character is visibly retained than in matched V3 rows.
No increase in product occlusion or camera-direction drift.
Close-up rows remain inside the frozen 0/1 local-prop and zero-background ceilings.
Wide rows remain inside three local props and two background anchors, with people unobtrusive and source-supported.
not_established_by_this_audit: That richer text will survive downstream rewriting
That more lexical cues will produce better images
That the four purposive renders generalize to all HP SKUs
